newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt to forecast '98 GDP growth of 2.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt to forecast '98 GDP growth of 2.0 pct.

text.p: Italy's forthcoming three-year programme of economic targets (DPEF) will forecast economic growth for 1998 of 2.0 percent, treasury and budget ministry undersecretary Giorgio Macciotta said on Friday.
The figure is a downwards revision from the 2.2 percent 1998 growth in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) forecast in official accounts published on March 20.

Macciotta told Reuters in a telephone interview that the DPEF document would forecast consumer price inflation for 1998 of 2.0 percent, unchanged from the previous estimate. Current forecasts for 1997 are of GDP growth of 1.2 percent and inflation of 2.5 percent.
The eagerly awaited DPEF, covering 1998-2000, is expected to give indications of savings the government hopes to make from a planned reform of the welfare state.
It will also give new 1998 deficit forecasts and will be used as the basis for Italy's convergence plan to join the European single currency.
Cabinet secretary Enrico Micheli said earlier that the document would probably be taken up at a cabinet meeting next week but this was not yet certain.
